texts: mixed: the Cauldron Hall link, the bedrock and 'below the building' are all right, but the location itself was emitted only as a per-cellar rule that lies dormant until some individual cellar is named — so 'where are the cellars?' currently answers nothing. Mark the cellars as one unit so the position is asserted of the whole set: 'The Cauldron Hall cellars lie together in the bedrock below the building.' (If they are really one connected space, the singular 'The Cauldron Hall cellar lies in the bedrock below the building' is cleaner still.)

good. the cellars come through as a group, 'hold' keeps them as the holder and the reserve as what is held, and 'large' stays a separate description; 'a reserve of mire-essence' lands on a generic of-link, which loses nothing.
good. each of the two properties is handed to every cellar separately, which is the reading you want.

good. this is the shape that parses best — one finite clause for the condition, one for the response, both subjects spelled out — and it yields a rule that fires whenever a Keeper stores a clay vessel.

mixed: 'before new vessels' has no verb of its own, so the parse had to guess the missing clause and reconstruct a second using event, and the result reads as two particular usings rather than a standing preference. Spell the second clause out: 'The Warden uses old vessels before the Warden uses new vessels.'
